title: Dates Out and the Share a Damage Finding Carries on Equipment Rental and Demo Kit
content:
## The rule

Kit that has been out on an Equipment Rental and Demo agreement for only a short time is worked at a heavier share of the package's replacement value than kit that has been out for a long one, because a fault found early is the more likely to have been done rather than worn.

Where the agreement's rental account carries fewer dates the kit was out than 4, the amount the finding carries is the light use share of the package's replacement value. The light use share is 22 per cent.

Where that account carries at least 4 such dates but fewer than 8, the amount the finding carries is the moderate use share of that replacement value instead. The moderate use share is 16 per cent.

In any other case nothing under this heading changes the share the finding carries.

## The two thresholds seen from both sides

| Dates the account carries for the kit being out | Share of the package's replacement value the finding carries |
| --- | --- |
| 0, 1, 2 or 3 | 22 per cent |
| 4 | 16 per cent |
| 5, 6 or 7 | 16 per cent |
| 8 | nothing under this heading |
| 9 or more | nothing under this heading |

The 4 is the hinge between the light band and the moderate band: 3 dates sits in the light band, 4 dates in the moderate band. The 8 is the hinge at the other end: 7 dates sits in the moderate band and 8 dates outside both.

## Worked figures on a hypothetical agreement

Take an agreement on a package whose replacement value is 890.00 USD.

- The account carries 3 dates the kit was out. The finding carries 22 per cent of 890.00 USD, which is 195.80 USD.
- The account carries 4 dates. The finding carries 16 per cent of 890.00 USD, which is 142.40 USD.
- The account carries 7 dates. The finding carries 16 per cent of 890.00 USD again, 142.40 USD.

Each of those figures is rounded half up to two decimal places, and the replacement value is the one held against the package the kit was hired on.

## Point of judgement

**What is counted.** What is counted is the dates the agreement's rental account carries for the kit being out, one for each date, and not the days the agreement was written for.
